What I heard in the Honourable Prosecutor's question, he was talking about a disciplinary infraction. I'm not a lawyer, that is different from a crime, but I've been trained between a disciplinary offence, a disciplinary infraction, and a crime. There are three kinds of offences.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, give us the name of one HVO soldier who was removed from military service, in any fashion, removed from military service for burning Bosnian Muslim houses. Give us the name of one.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I already told this Honourable Court that I was at the level of commander of an Operative Zone. I did not have an inventory of names. I already said that if I look at the first three months, I can only see the figure of 92 crimes having been committed in my Operative Zone. Among these 92 crimes, I believe that there might have been such crimes too, but I didn't look into that because this was up to the district military court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us continue, General. In June of 1994, you took command of an operation called Operation Pauk which you say you wanted to expand to investigate and prosecute war crimes. Do you recall that testimony in response to questions by my learned colleague, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During your zealous investigation and prosecution of war crimes, give us the name of one HVO soldier who was prosecuted under Operation Pauk for the burning of Bosnian Muslim houses in the Central Bosnia Operative Zone. Give us the name of one.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: You see, again, you're putting a question to me that pertains to a name. I was head of the operation called Pauk, and we were looking into all forms of unlawfulness. We also wanted to have a broader basis for looking into war crimes. I had assistants who each had their own line of work, and they worked as best they could under the circumstances. But I did not have a list of individual names concerning these details. This is a big file and everybody has work of his own. Because military courts are not under military commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us complete our analysis of the state of affairs in Busovaca as we move into late January 1993. Leaving off from the Mijo Bozic order from the 27th of January, let us turn finally to Prosecutor's Exhibit 472.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is an under-seal document. It should not be placed on the ELMO. Is this a Defence exhibit or Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Prosecution. Excuse me, Counsel, if I can ask for a clarification. Your records reflect that this is an under-seal document? For us, it does not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: D472 is under seal. We'll check P472.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Okay. Our records don't reflect it as such, Judge, but it's better to check, and if we can just check one more time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Let's make sure.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No. This is a public document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If this is a public document, then we will remain in open session. Can we see this document, please? I have your document, Mr. Registrar, your copy. All right. Mr. Kehoe, does the witness have the document before him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I believe so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, this is a document that was written to you by your chief of staff, Franjo Nakic. Let us reflect on the state of affairs in Busovaca, and if we could turn to the second page, Mr. Usher, under "Agenda." "Implementation of conclusions from Kiseljak. "Mr. Stewart said that he did not blame any side for the violation of the cease-fire, but the reports he received indicated that it was the HVO who were the ones who started it." The comments of Mr. Fleming: "When attempting to stop the fighting, Mr. Fleming was denied access Busovaca by the HVO; he had to remain outside as he was not allowed to enter the town. "His vehicle was shot at an HVO checkpoint. "The BH Army gave him its full cooperation. "Mr. Stewart made the comment that God had saved him from a mortar shell fired by the HVO (it came from the HVO side). "Mr. Fleming was full of praise for the 3rd Corps Command, I quote: 'They are doing great things for peace.' He has evidence, even in writing as they send correspondence in English and meet him on a daily basis. The BH Army has submitted lists of Croatian prisoners held in Zenica and Kacuni. They have also given him permission in writing to visit prisoners while the HVO has not done anything and will not allow visits to prisoners." General, you were aware of these facts while you were in Kiseljak on the 30th of January, 1993, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I believe that I received this report, but it is quite clear from this report that I was isolated, blocked in Kiseljak and that I was not meeting Mr. Fleming every day. On the 30th of January, I didn't even know him, that is to say, I was sealed off in Kiseljak. But in my order, already from the 27th of January, I ordered that all prisoners be released in keeping with the regulations of the International Red Cross. However, may I comment on this document? On page 2, where Mr. Merdan is mentioned in relation to the shelling of Zenica, because yesterday we talked about the shelling of Merdani and another village --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, General. We can discuss those during redirect examination. My next question on this score is this: You were informed on the 30th of January that your troops were not cooperating with international agencies and also were preventing them from visiting prisoners; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, that is not right. Already on the 26th -- on the 25th of January in the morning, I asked the UNPROFOR headquarters for Bosnia-Herzegovina in Kiseljak to mediate in the organisation of a meeting between myself and the commander of the 3rd Corps, and, indeed, that is what they did. But on the 26th of January, 1993, instead of the commander of the 3rd Corps, Dzemo Merdan arrived. The problem was that I believed that Mr. Fleming did not even know that I was isolated and cut off from my command and that I could not give operative orders to the forces in Vitez and Busovaca. I did not have any communications. I was totally cut off in Kiseljak. I believed that I would have been at this meeting in Vitez, not my chief of staff, had I been in a position to come or had I been invited.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: During this period of time, you were in contact with Dario Kordic, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: In telephone contact with the commander of the brigades in Busovaca and with Dario Kordic, yes, I was. In that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let us reflect once again on Prosecutor's Exhibit 629. This is a document that we spoke of previously, General, of 2 February, 1993, a press release by the Party for Democratic Action, the Muslim party in Vitez. We'll reference the date. The date is 2 February, 1993, and it notes that: "In an interview with Dario Kordic, the vice-president of the so-called HZ /Croatian Community/ of Herceg-Bosna, aired on HZ Herceg-Bosna TV for Studio Vitez on 1 February 1993, it was stated among other things that both the Muslims and Bosnia and Herzegovina will cease to exist." I'd like to direct our attention to the actual video and translation of those particular comments as elicited or enunciated by Mr. Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, this, of course, is the tape that was placed with the video booth.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As for the tape, it will be Prosecution Exhibit 679, and the transcript of that same tape will be Exhibit 679/1 for the B/C/S version and 679/2 for the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you want to have this tape played, Mr. Kehoe?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's just several minutes long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Fine. Mr. Kehoe, do the booths have a transcript of this tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I have some extra copies, Mr. President. I can do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's best to proceed in that way before playing the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. I would also like to correct what I said. Exhibit 679/1 is the B/C/S version, 679/2 for the French version, as I have just seen that there's a French version, and 679/3 for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In the booth, if we could rewind that, please, just to start from the beginning, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I will remind everybody that I do have a French version of what is about to be played, and I thank you for that, Mr. Kehoe, but I think it will also allow the interpreters to go about this more comfortably. All right. I think every booth now has its own copy of the transcript, so do the Judges, so the technician's booth can start playing the tape. Thank you. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: (Voiceover) "JOURNALIST: In Central Bosnia and Busovaca "DARIO KORDIC: Today, while we are talking, General Morillon is discussing several issues with the two highest commanders for Central Bosnia in Vitez: HVO Commander of the Operations Area in Central Bosnia, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, and the war criminal, Commander of the 3rd Muslim Corps, Enver Hadzihasanovic. The HVO is asking that the cease-fire agreement signed two days ago be respected, roads for humanitarian convoys opened, which have already been agreed. The HVO is asking that telephone lines for Busovaca which the Zenica local authorities have disconnected be reconnected. The HVO is asking power be turned on. Other agreeable issues are being discussed. I am certain that our side will be cooperative, and our men have been given the order not to fire a single bullet. Furthermore, we will not return fire if our positions are shelled. Should there be infantry attacks, we will certainly defend ourselves. However, I have to express my personal suspicions as regards Muslim forces. I am not certain that the Muslim forces will not attempt to play the same scenario - if not in Busovaca, then in some other area - within the next ten or fifteen days. The reason is that, apparently, they have chosen a war option by refusing to negotiate in Geneva under the given conditions. They want to seize as much territory as possible to the detriment of the Croatian population because they realised they failed to seize territory from the Serb aggressor. They believe it is easier with the Croats and that this is feasible. To their deep regret, I am once again warning the Muslim population: 'Do not play with fire. If you attack other municipalities, not only that there will be no Bosnia-Herzegovina, but there will be no Muslims left.' "JOURNALIST: Mr. Kordic, thank you "MR. KORDIC: Thank you too."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this conversation or this interview with Kordic is taking place while you are in Vitez at the British Battalion talking to General Morillon; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is right. But may I just explain how this came about, how come I was in Vitez and how come the meeting was called with General Morillon chairing it? That is an essential point. When I saw that the agreement of the 27th of January, 1993 was not being implemented, I personally requested and demanded that General Morillon extend his assistance to me and to mediate between me, as the commander, and the commander of the 3rd Corps, to hold another meeting so as to agree upon the implementation of what we had previously agreed upon, that is to say, the agreement of the 27th of January, 1993. I asked for and initiated that meeting and I was taken to the meeting, transported by the U.N. forces to the U.N. base in Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, at this time, Dario Kordic is the senior political official in Central Bosnia; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Dario Kordic was the top political official in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: He issues a threat to the Bosnian Muslims that if there is any additional attack on other municipalities, there will neither be any Bosnia and Herzegovina, nor will there be any Muslims. My question for you is, General, these are not comments that would promote peaceful negotiations, would they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course, they are not comments which it is pleasant to hear or which are desirable. But you see here, we have one situation in Busovaca where there is a conflict. In Vitez, from the document you gave me, 629, a joint government is being talked about and a unified MUP, and the Muslims have every protection. So in three municipalities, with a space of ten kilometres between them, we have different situations. In one, fighting; in another, complete protection; in the third, an agreement to transcend tensions in Busovaca. So three municipalities within a range of ten kilometres and radically different situations in each one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, once again, we have a situation where one arm of the HVO is negotiating for the cessation of hostilities and the other arm simultaneously is threatening the entire elimination of the Bosnian Muslim population in the area; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: The civilian part and the message we heard, I already said that that is a sort of threat but that it was not -- that I was not bound by any statements made by politicians. I had my chain of command from the main staff. However, from the entire context, talks are mentioned here and everything else, what was happening in Vitez and so on in the document that you gave us. The document is number 679/3. As I say, there were different statements made by different politicians.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let us go and continue on in Busovaca and study the condition of the Muslims shortly after this statement in mid-February.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can go to this next document, Mr. Usher. This is a military information summary, Mr. President, Your Honours, of the British Battalion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: One question, General Blaskic. Mr. Kordic is not any political leader, and you were, in a sense, subordinated to him, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I was not subordinated to him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: But when we listen to you, we have the impression that Mr. Kordic, the political leader is saying something whereas you, the military man, you are doing much as you please.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Mr. President, I was working exclusively according to the commands of the chief of the main staff of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Mr. Kehoe, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 680.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, General, this is a military information summary of 11 February, 1993, and if I could go to the third page, Mr. Usher, under "Busovaca." Now, General, this is ten days after Kordic's statements, and I read you as follows, in point 5, Busovaca: "The HVO Brigade in Busovaca is now commanded by Dusko Grubesic. The previous commander is reported to have moved to the HVO Brigade in Zepce. Reports from 1 Cheshire LO," that means liaison officer, "indicates that the Muslims living within Busovaca are subject to a strict curfew and are basically housebound within their own community." Is that true, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already stated that I was not in a position, operationally speaking, to issue commands and monitor the situation in Busovaca because I was isolated. It was not the commander of the HVO Brigade from Busovaca that was replaced. He could not take up his duties at all. That is to say, on the 21st of January, 1993, after a regular meeting, the commander of the brigade from Busovaca asked me for him to go to visit his family, to go off on a weekend. He went to Zepce. And you go to Zepce via Zenica. When the conflict broke out, he was not able to return to take up his duties in Busovaca again. He was not able to do so because the BH army would not have allowed him to do so, and it was in control of Zenica. That is an indicator of the extent to which we find ourselves caught up by all the events in Busovaca. So the commander of Busovaca was isolated in Zepce, where I myself was isolated in Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, you were getting information from your chief of staff, Franjo Nakic, that we saw in Prosecutor's 472, were you not?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I was receiving daily reports, but I don't see a stamp here when this was received. Sometimes they would be as much as two days late. And I said operative command, in real-time, I was not able to carry out in the Busovaca and Vitez areas. I did receive a report on the 26th of January which spoke about the lack of communication between Kiseljak and Vitez.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So my question for you, General, is: For the Muslims population as of the 11th of February or thereafter, were the Muslims subject to a strict curfew and basically housebound in their own community? That's a fact; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have said that information of this kind did not reach me except for summaries of daily information on combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, let's turn to information that you told us about. You told us, General, that on the 2nd of March of 1993, you were informed that 60 per cent of the Muslims wanted to leave the Kiseljak municipality. Do you recall telling us that? The page reference, for record-keeping purposes is 18339. Do you recall that, General?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Of course I recall that. It was a report from the civilian authorities and the council for national defence of Kiseljak. I believe that the reason for the concern on the part of the Muslims was that on the territory of the Kiseljak municipality and the local community of Bilalovac, there had been a persecution of Croats, and in the area a new municipality was being set up which was under the leadership of the wartime presidency composed of Bosniak Muslims from the Kiseljak region. I believe that the Bosniak Muslim people in the Kiseljak municipality became worried as to how the civilian and other HVO authorities would react to conduct of this kind when in one municipality another municipality was, in fact, being formed, but, luckily, those 60 per cent of Bosniak Muslims did not leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, let us shift gears for one moment and take a look again at Prosecutor's Exhibit 657. That is the order of President Jadranko Prlic of the 15th of January, 1993. Now, we have looked at this document previously, General, and I want to focus your attention on paragraph 1 especially. I take that back. Paragraph 1 and 2, where it reads: "1. All units of the Bosnia and Herzegovina army currently in regions 3, 8, and 10, which were proclaimed Croatian in the Geneva agreements, are subordinate to the command of the main headquarters of the HVO armed forces. "2. All units of the HVO armed forces currently in regions 1, 5, and 9, which were proclaimed Muslim in the Geneva agreements, are subordinate to the command of the General staff of the Bosnia and Herzegovina army command." Now, with regard to those two provisions, what does this order contemplate?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I have already spoken about this decision, and especially this order in document 657. I said that I had seen it for the first time in the courtroom. It never reached me. For me it has no importance. I acted according to orders from the chief of the main staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sorry. General, I understand that. I'm talking about what does this order contemplate? As you read this order, as a military man, what does this order contemplate? If you don't understand that question, I will clarify.

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Both sides subordination of HVO units and the BH army, that is to say, that the units of the BH army, in provinces 3, 8, and 10 should be subordinated to the command of the main staff of the armed forces and that the units of the armed forces of the HVO in provinces 1, 5, and 9 be subordinated to the command of the General staff of the BH army. However, for my Operative Zone that could not be implemented. There is no commander who, under such circumstances, would be able to implement such a thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: So, General, suffice it to say that the bottom line is that this order contemplates that BH army units in regions 3, 8, and 10 would be placed under HVO command and HVO units in 1, 5, and 9 would be placed under BiH command. Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. With the proviso that this is on the basis of the order of the Minister of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Bozo Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This particular order is a subordination order; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This order is about subordination and not attachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, let us discuss -- we talked about the events during January of Busovaca, and we talked about the events in Gornji Vakuf in January. Let us talk about what is taking place in another locale in the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna at the same time, and that is Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I would like to move to the next exhibit, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 681, 681A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, let us work until 12.25, for another ten minutes, and then we'll have a 20-minute break, and we can have 45 minutes after that to work until the end of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is everybody ready? Mr. Prosecutor, could you tell us briefly what it's about and may we have your questions, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. This is an information circular that was produced by the commander of the 4th Corps, Arif Pasalic, the commander of the 4th Corps of the army of Bosnia-Hezegovina, where he describes what is taking place during January of 1993, the same time frame that we've been talking about, except this particular issue deals with Mostar, Mr. President. "Information about the situation and the problems which the HVO of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna is causing for members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Muslim people. "The purpose of this text is for the world to find out the real truth about the various kinds of pressures exerted by the HVO of the so-called Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The text is brief for practical reasons and everything we say in it is supported by evidence which can be produced for inspection at any time. "During the first days of the war, when battles were being fought for liberation from the aggressor, the HVO took overpower, promising to cooperate with the units of the former Territorial Defence. On the night of fighting to liberate the left bank of the Neretva River in Mostar, not a single HVO unit crossed over to the left bank of the Neretva River to help the soldiers of the independent battalion (of the then Mostar Territorial Defence). "With the take-over of power by the HVO, gradual inclusion into the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna began. From that time on there was pressure, slight at first but stepped up at certain times. "First, the replacement of directors and leading local figures was carried out on a mass scale. Only people from the HVO and ethnic Croats were appointed. "There was a ban on receiving and accommodating refugees and an order was issued that they should go to the area of Zenica (and the reason for this has now become evident). All important buildings were taken over by force and property was plundered, appropriated and taken to Western Herzegovina. The city was decked out in Croatian flags, while flags of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were taken down. Justice and administration were placed at the service of HZ HB and a parallel system of justice and administration was set up which led to parallel authorities in this region. Everything that was enacted by the legal bodies of the recognised state of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was set aside and could not be implemented. Real anarchy has been created in this domain. "Internal affairs and the police were taken over in a surprise move and placed in the service of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. Regulations were enacted in this domain which ran counter to the regulations of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and officers of Croatian nationality were appointed. In this way, the security of citizens and their property was undermined because the commission of criminal offences in the city and the surrounding area was permitted and the perpetrators were put under the protection of the HVO. "Education was discontinued, although most schools could have been adapted for reaching relatively quickly. This culminated in the recent establishment of a Croatian university. In Mostar in Zagreb the university is called..." and the rest of the page is missing. The next page, Mr. Usher. "In all domains of life and work the HZ HB is looking for solutions outside the existing legislation of the Republic of BH, and all official documents bear the Croatian coat of arms and not the coat of arms of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As regards cultural institutions, nothing has been done except for the establishment of Croatian associations (the Zrinski football club) and the renaming of Mostar streets with Croatian names. "The issue of refugees has not been adequately dealt with. There are about 18.000 refugees, mostly from Eastern Herzegovina. They are accommodated in a way that is below human dignity and many of them are staying with relatives. During the summer, the HZ HB issued an order that they should be moved to the Zenica area. "Health care is organised through the war hospital of the HVO HZ HB, and the staff were pressured into taking an oath. Those who did not take the oath did not receive their salaries. The head people are of Croatian nationality. "At first there was an information blockade in Mostar, and the HVO imposed a biased system of information. Members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina started their own media, but we were hindered in various ways ranging from censorship to a forcible cutting off of power at one time. "All means are used to prevent people from watching the TV programmes of the Republic of BH, although the conditions for this are in place. "The economy is in chaos. The procedure for appointing government commissioners and authorised representatives in companies was established by a decision of the HVO government, while decision and decrees of the Republic of BH are not respected. "The financial and monetary system is the Croatian dinar. According to the decision issued by HZ HB, the legal currency of the Republic of BH is not valid here. An attempt was made to introduce the legal currency of the Republic of BH but this was prohibited. "The traffic system is practically paralysed. About 60 buses belonging to the Autoprevoz company in Mostar were taken to Siroki Brijeg, and these assets were stolen at the order of the HZ HB and given to private entrepreneurs to transport passengers and goods on the Western Herzegovina-Germany route for their own profit and the profit of the HZ HB. Besides this plunder, the government of the HVO HZ HB illegally replaced the traffic administration. "In parallel with these other pressures, the post and telecommunications system has been disrupted, although the switchboard (six-digit) is not out of order. Only a few select people from the HVO HZ HB have telephone connections. "All the conditions exist for the building of Mostar and for traffic and railway transport but the HVO HZ HB refuses to allow work on the bridges, for reasons known only to them. "They are also preventing town planning and reconstruction. "Besides all this, other kinds of pressure are being exerted on the people, including HVO identity cards for civilians, permission to leave the city and to go to the Republic of Croatia. Everything has been put under HVO HZ HB control. Documents have to be paid for and documents of the army of the Republic of BH are not recognised. "Objects, personal property, weapons, ammunition, and vehicles are confiscated, and Muslims who are members of the army of the Republic of BH are arrested. "Housing problems are solved only for members of the HVO. In spite of numerous pleas, on 18 January, 1993 they gave only a few flats to the members of the army of the Republic of BH who had been killed. "Out of the 705 flats abandoned by members of the former JNA, the First Mostar Brigade is given 73 flats for the families of those killed and 10 for the seriously disabled. The HVO is giving the other flats to families of the HVO members who have been killed, the wounded officers, soldiers, and other members of the HVO. This partial way of resolving housing issues is leading to chaos and is causing one of the burning problems in the brigade, i.e., the eviction of the members of the First Mostar Brigade of the army of BH and many Muslim refugees and citizens whose refugee housing status has not yet been resolved. Citizens and soldiers alike are being thrown out on to the street. All the abandoned flats in Mostar are at the disposal of the HVO. "So far, many members of the army and the Muslim people have been arrested and dozens of them are still in prison. Besides this, foreign nationals working on providing aid to everyone, and not only Muslims, are being arrested. The foreign nationals Hasan Ebu and Galib Esafi, officials of Igasa, have been in prison since November. When they were arrested, their vehicle and more than 800.000 Deutschmarks (and in various currencies) was confiscated from them. There are four members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina from Prozor and one from Mostar in prison in Grude. We have been requesting their release several times. Their names are Mirsad Vugdalic, Ramo Bektes, Mirsad Gorancic, Sofet Sefer, and Nedir Pejzic. "The property of members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and of the Muslim people is being plundered and looted daily. All weapons, ammunition, food, personal belongings, and money are being seized and all this is taken to Western Herzegovina and the HVO barracks. "They have confiscated eight mortars, 90.000 pieces of ammunition of various calibres, a large quantity of rifles, pistols, and ammunition for these, and 2.000 shells of various types. "Dozens of vehicles have been confiscated together with their cargo. Besides that, death threats have been made daily against certain leading figures in the army of the Republic of BH. "In recent days, these pressures have culminated in the order issued about the HZ HB that the units of the army of the Republic of BH are to be resubordinated to the HVO and the order for the total blockade of the borders of the so-called HZ HB. On that occasion, numerous convoys of trucks carrying humanitarian aid to Bosnia were stopped. These trucks are now in Posusje, Grude, Ljubuski, and Mostar. The goods on the trucks are being looted. "At the moment, there are over 40 trucks at the Heliodrom, with humanitarian aid and with the documents in order. The drivers have been released but they were mistreated in various ways when the trucks were being confiscated. The goods from the trucks are being looted on a large scale. "As of January 1993, the following vehicles have been confiscated." In the original there is a list of numerous vehicles here that have not been re-translated here but are in the original document. "These are only some of the instances of pressure, and we reiterate that all this is documented and can be made available. "To make matters worse, all logistical support to members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina has been cut off by the HVO since midsummer 1992. "Commander of the 4th Corps of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Mr. Arif Pasalic."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe. I assume you have a number of questions to put to the witness on that document. We'll take a 20-minute break and then we'll resume our work and do so until 1.30. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please be seated. Mr. Kehoe, just before the break, you read this very long document which comes from the 4th Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Would you now like to go on to the questions you want to put to the witness about this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, based on what you know of the events in Mostar, the HVO, up through this letter in January of 1993, took control over all of the municipal authorities in Mostar, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was only one municipality in Mostar. Perhaps there were more, but I don't know. The question was put to me in the following way, whether the HVO took control over all the municipal authorities in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's correct. The municipal authorities in Mostar, as of January of 1993, were controlled by the HVO; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not have any direct information, apart from what I heard here from this document, and I did not discuss this situation with the author of the document. He speaks of an entire spectrum of civilian issues. I do not have any knowledge about this, but I would like to comment on the document, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, General, do you have any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No. I think the question was very precise. You are not aware of that, it was a civilian matter, you had no knowledge about it, so I think, Mr. Kehoe, you can go on to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, General, did, in fact, the HVO take control of the entire spectrum of civilian life in the Mostar municipality by January of 1993? To your knowledge, did they do so?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know that the situation was rather chaotic and that it varied from one environment to another. We heard all about Mostar from this document, and all of this can be said of Sarajevo as well. I imagine that in this kind of chaotic situation, the civilian structures wanted to take over as many functions as possible. Where extremist individuals were in power, they tried to strengthen their own authority as much as possible and to accomplish their objectives as much as possible, but this is, generally speaking, a chaotic situation which varies only to the extent to who is in a dominant position. In Sarajevo, it was the Bosniak Muslims, but there was a state of chaos.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mostar was declared to be the capital of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. That is just what I've been saying, that these problems were a general phenomenon which depended on who was dominant. In Mostar, there was a situation, but there was a similar situation in Sarajevo, depending on whether the HVO or the BH army was predominant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: General, you noted for us, in looking at the orders of Jadranko Prlic, that his order contemplated that there would be a resubordination of BH army units to the HVO and the HVO units to the BiH in various cantons. Let's take a look at the second or third paragraph on page 4, if we can, Mr. Usher, and in the English version, it is the bottom of page 3. On the bottom of your page -- excuse me. On the top of your page 4, General, the third paragraph down, again, this is the bottom of page 3 in the English, it notes: "In recent days, these pressures have culminated in the order issued by HZ HB that units of the army of the Republic of BH are to be resubordinated to the HVO and the order for the total blockade of the borders of the so-called HZ HB." I would ask you to examine the word "resubordinate," and if we could take a look at Exhibit 666 once again. General, the word that General Pasalic uses for resubordination is the same word that Milivoj Petkovic uses to describe the Vitezovi's relationship to you, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, the word is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, pursuant to your request, the Office of the Prosecutor, as well as with the assistance of counsel, have attempted to resolve the questions pertaining to Exhibit 657, 658, and 659 which were the sequential orders. We have two articles from Oslobodenje, a periodical from Sarajevo, and then an article that was provided by counsel which is a British Broadcasting summary excerpt from Croatian Radio. If we can go through those in seriatim, we will provide the Chamber with as much information as we have at this particular juncture. If we can start with the first article which is the Oslobodenje article of the 18th of January, 1993. I do have some for the booths as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We would ask, Mr. President, that the translation on Prosecutor's Exhibit 681A be corrected, just as the translation yesterday was corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Counsel. I think we can address this during your cross-examination. But, Mr. President, the fact remains that the witness testified this morning that what was contemplated by Prlic's order was a subordination, not an attachment, a subordination. Low and behold, what we see in this particular document from Pasalic is the word "resubordination," which is the same word that is used in the document that Milivoj Petkovic uses on the 19th of January in Exhibit 666.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: But not in the original, Mr. President. You can translate a document anyhow you please, but this is the same word we were discussing yesterday and we referred to the translators.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You will address this issue within your right to rejoinder, Mr. Hayman. We shall go on. Yes. What is this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 682, Prosecution Exhibit 682, 682A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is again some attempt to clarify some of the chronology here by these two articles in Oslobodenje. This one first is dated the 18th of January, 1993 entitled "Open Attempt at Annexation." "Subject: 1993 HVO order to take over territories under BH army control." I will read it very slowly, Mr. President. The booths do have a copy. "The Staff of the RBH OS /Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina/ and the Supreme Command was informed on 15 January 1993 about the unilateral and in no way provoked decision of the HVO /Croatian Defence Council/ of the so-called "Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna" and the order of the head of the HVO department in Mostar. The above-mentioned decision orders that units of the RBH Army which are in the areas designated in the Geneva agreements as the possible provinces 3, 8 and 10 should be subordinated to the command of the HVO Main Staff. By prejudicing and interpreting in a separatist manner the Geneva negotiations, an attempt is being made to set up these possible provinces militarily and define them as a separate Croatian territory within the internationally recognised and sovereign State of Bosnia and Herzegovina. "The ultimatum-like attempt to treat these legal units of the RBH Army as paramilitary formations in the unified territory of the republic if they refuse this subordination is completely at odds with the common struggle against the Chetnik aggressor, as well as with the thousand-year-old tradition of the tolerant coexistence of the Muslim and Croatian peoples. The risky and in the long term very dangerous attempt to take military possession of areas which are the subject of the negotiations in Geneva is a serious attack on the talks about the future order in Bosnia and Herzegovina and at the same time represents an open attempt to annex its territories for the sake of expansionist concepts and ideas. "Bearing in mind that attempts are being made to misuse and manipulate the negotiations in Geneva before they are even over, the Staff of the RBH OS Supreme Command is of the opinion that the above-mentioned decision of the HVO Main Staff is a direct threat to the territorial integrity of the BH State and truly contrary to the collective wishes and interests of the Croatian population which lives in Bosnia and Herzegovina and which is predominantly pro-Bosnian in orientation. "Therefore, the Staff of the RBH OS Supreme Command also considers as completely unacceptable the order of the yet-to-be officially inaugurated Defence Minister Bozo Rajic wherein he treats units of the RBH and the HVO in the same way as the aggressor's Chetnik army, and incompetently orders them to retreat individually to the lines of the imagined provinces, i.e., to the imagined State borders of the three States within the only recognised State of Bosnia and Herzegovina. For the Staff of the RBH OS Supreme Command and for all the fighters who are fighting for a single, sovereign, indivisible, equal and democratic Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mr. Rajic's order is a non-binding act and a manipulation of the collective misfortune of the Muslims and Croats, caused by the same aggressor. "Therefore, it is quite logical that immediately after the statement by the HVO of the 'HZ /Croatian Community/ of Herceg-Bosna,' the Chief of Staff of the RBH OS Supreme Command issued the following order to all commands, staffs..." and then is the particular order given by Sefer Halilovic, which I'll gladly read, Mr. President, but -- I will continue to read it. "1. Commands, staffs, units and institutions of the RBH Army must not accept decisions of the HVO of the 'HZ Herceg-Bosna'" "... but must act exclusively on the decisions of the Staff of the RBH OS Supreme Command. "2. In the zones of responsibility measures should be taken to implement further cooperation with HVO units and to prevent conflicts between HVO and the BH Army. Extremist behaviour by individuals and groups in the BH Army directed at HVO members must be prevented. In the event of threats to RBH Army members and units by extremist HVO members, a warning should be issued first, and energetic action to protect the lives of individuals and units taken afterwards. At the same time, care should be taken not to weaken defensive positions towards the aggressor. "3. An assessment of the present situation and possible conflicts relating to the decisions by the HVO of the so-called 'HZ Herceg-Bosna' should be carried out and all measures taken to prevent such conflicts, says the order of the Chief of Staff of the RBH OS Supreme Command Sefer Halilovic, which concludes the press release of the RBH Army Press Centre."

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: The next document, Mr. President, is a follow-up chronologically, and this document again is an Oslobodenje document, much shorter in length, of the 20th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 683, 683A for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: As I noted, Mr. President, this is, again, an Oslobodenje article from 20 January, 1993. It's concerning a joint session of the BH presidency and government. The date is Sarajevo, 19 January. "The HVO continues," there is some question, "building up strong forces from Western Herzegovina in the Gornji Vakuf area, and provocations and clashes show no sign of abating. "This was concluded at today's joint session of the presidency and the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In addition, a statement from the session pointed out that the aim of the HVO activities was to prejudice by military means, i.e., by force, decisions of the Geneva conference and to present its participants with a fait accompli. "'Unless the HVO promptly eases armed operations, the BH government proposes that the BH presidency take appropriate measures in the U.N. Security Council to establish the responsibility of the Republic of Croatia for its evident involvement in the escalation of the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina,' the statement from the joint session emphasised. "The BH presidency and government offered their full support to the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina to persist in its struggle and appeal to all citizens who hold Bosnia and Herzegovina dear to join in these efforts. "At the same time, the BH presidency and government have announced that the order of Bozo Rajic on the resubordination of the BH army units to the HVO in certain areas of BH has absolutely no basis in law and as such is null and void. Decisions of this kind, under the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, fall exclusively within the jurisdiction of the presidency of the republic, not of the Minister of Defence. Furthermore, the newly appointed Defence Minister in the BH government has not taken the oath or assumed office. "In view of the political and military situation in the Republic, the presidency and government have requested that BH Prime Minister Mile Akmadzic to return immediately to Sarajevo and assume his duties." The last media report on this subject, in our possession at this time, is a media report that Mr. Hayman offered to the court, and that has to do with a media report on the 16th of January -- actually, it's published on the 18th but it refers to Croatian radio on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit 684.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: This, unfortunately, is just in English, Mr. President. There is no B/C/S copy. It is, as I noted, a summary, a BBC summary of world broadcasts. The summary is dated 18 January, 1993, and it reflects a broadcast that came on the Croatian radio in Zagreb at 18.00 on 16 January, 1993. That's 18.00 Greenwich Mean Time. I'm not sure what the time difference is between Zagreb and Greenwich Mean Time. In any event, the body of the text of the report: "The Defence Minister of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bozo Rajic, today issued an order which says, among other things: "All units of the HVO which at the moment are positioned in provinces one, five, and nine, which the Geneva negotiations proclaimed to be Muslim provinces, will come under the control of the main headquarters of the Bosnia and Herzegovina army. All units of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army, which at the moment are positioned in provinces three, eight, and ten, which the Geneva negotiations proclaimed to be Croatian provinces, will come under the control of the main headquarters of the HVO. All units of the Serbian Republic and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are to withdraw their personnel and equipment into provinces two, four, and six, which the Geneva negotiations proclaimed to be Serbian provinces. All units of the HVO, the Bosnia-Herzegovina army and the Serbian army, which are at the moment positioned in province ten (sic), for which the Geneva negotiation" -- province 7, excuse me, "in province seven, for which the Geneva negotiations envisaged special status must unconditionally cease all hostilities. "All points in this order will remain in force until the final agreement is signed and a new decision on the implementation of the Geneva peace agreement reached." So from the sequence of these documents we have, 687, 688 and 689 -- excuse me, 657, 658, and 659 signed by Prlic, Stojic, and Petkovic on the 15th, and this particular document reflects the announcement by Bozo Rajic on the 16th, one day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: By way of clarification, General, Bozo Rajic ultimately became the Minister of Defence for the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Bozo Rajic, as far as I know, did not become Minister of Defence of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna. The Minister of Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, rather, that's what he was. I do not know of him ever being Minister of Defence of the Croat Community of Herceg-Bosna or was he ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Was Bruno Stojic replaced in 1994 as Minister of Defence of the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Sorry, could you please repeat the date? I didn't get the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: In 1994, was Bruno Stojic replaced as the Defence Minister for the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, he was replaced. He was replaced, Bruno Stojic was replaced too, and other cadre. That's what President Boban decided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did Bruno Stojic have another position in that government, in the Croatian Republic of Herceg-Bosna government at that time?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know whether he did at that time because this is the civilian sector, but I do know that for a certain period of time he was director of the news agency. It was called Habena. Then during that period whether he had a post or not, I don't know. But he did have a post in the government but, at any rate, he was never Minister of Defence of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Bozo Rajic was a Croat; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: TIHOMIR BLASKIC (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, Bozo Rajic is a Croat. I already spoke of the division of various ministries and posts in the government, and I said that in the government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina the Minister of Defence was a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, by way of clarification, that is the information we have at this time on the sequence of events involving 657, 658, and 659. If we have any other information that we can gather, certainly we will bring it to the court's attention. I will acknowledge the assistance of Mr. Hayman in providing the last article which he did provide for the court for its review.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well then. Well, the Judges do thank the Defence counsel for their explanation on this particularly important issue. It is now 1.32. We will adjourn the hearing, the last hearing for this week. We will resume our work on the 17th at 2.00 in the afternoon. The hearing is adjourned.
